newsitem.title: USA: Hair-braiders in a dander over NY licensing rules.
newsitem.headline: Hair-braiders in a dander over NY licensing rules.

text.p: Two African-style hair braiders have sued New York state over its required 900 hours of study to qualify for a license, alleging they are being forced to learn unrelated skills from shaving to resume writing.

The suit, filed in New York State Supreme Court in Manhattan, alleges the curriculum requirement infringes on the plaintiffs' right to pursue an occupation free from "arbitrary and capricious government interference."
The plaintiffs seek a court ruling declaring the licensing requirement unconstitutional under state and federal law.

Andrean Russell and Bonnie Best, both of New York City, said in the suit the requirement for a natural hair-styling license provides that they must take 200 hours of hair-cutting training even though braiders do not cut hair and 160 hours of hairstyling that covers techniques they do not use.
They said they must also study how to shave faces and carry out certain business practices such as resume and letter writing.
